message:
## Vulnerability Digest

**Scan window:** 2026-11-07 05:10 IST to 2026-11-08 05:10 IST (2026-11-06 23:40 to 2026-11-07 23:40 UTC)  
**Scope:** Combined and deduplicated entries from `Products.txt` and `List_of_SIA_Completed.txt` only; `DLL_software_component.txt` was not read or combined.

Four newly published CVEs were verified against two monitored products: one critical Keycloak server issue and three low-severity Advanced Custom Fields issues. Four upstream Linux SMB CVEs are listed separately as possible matches because their applicability to monitored Ubuntu builds is not yet confirmed.

### Finding 1 — Keycloak server code execution

- **Product:** Keycloak / Red Hat Build of Keycloak
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-120984
- **Severity:** CVSS 9.1 Critical; Red Hat rates the product impact Important because exploitation requires authenticated client-management permissions.
- **Description:** Keycloak can retain an internal setup-session attribute when a client with authorization services is created or imported. A privileged client manager could use this to upload a malicious JavaScript policy that executes on the server during an authorization request.
- **Relevance:** Keycloak is explicitly present in the monitored product list.
- **Source:** [Red Hat CVE record](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2026-120984) and [CVE/NVD-backed summary](https://www.tenable.com/cve/CVE-2026-120984)

### Finding 2 — ACF unpublished-post metadata disclosure

- **Product:** Advanced Custom Fields (ACF) for WordPress
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-97189
- **Severity:** Low, CVSS 2.7
- **Description:** A contributor-level or higher user can use relational fields to learn titles and non-public statuses of unpublished posts they cannot otherwise view.
- **Relevance:** Advanced Custom Fields is explicitly monitored; versions before 6.8.11 are affected.
- **Source:** [CVE record details](https://app.opencve.io/cve/CVE-2026-97189) and [ACF 6.8.11 security release](https://www.advancedcustomfields.com/blog/acf-6-8-11-security-release/)

### Finding 3 — ACF relationship-field authorization bypass

- **Product:** Advanced Custom Fields (ACF) for WordPress
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-97190
- **Severity:** Low, CVSS 2.7
- **Description:** A contributor-level or higher user can alter bidirectional relationship references on posts, users, or terms they are not permitted to edit.
- **Relevance:** Advanced Custom Fields is explicitly monitored; versions 6.2.0 through 6.8.10 are affected.
- **Source:** [CVE record details](https://app.opencve.io/cve/CVE-2026-97190) and [ACF 6.8.11 security release](https://www.advancedcustomfields.com/blog/acf-6-8-11-security-release/)

### Finding 4 — ACF restricted-field write bypass

- **Product:** Advanced Custom Fields (ACF) for WordPress
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-97191
- **Severity:** Low, CVSS 2.7
- **Description:** A contributor-level or higher user can submit custom-field values that the site's field-group location rules intended to reserve for administrators.
- **Relevance:** Advanced Custom Fields is explicitly monitored; versions before 6.8.11 are affected.
- **Source:** [CVE record details](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-97191) and [ACF 6.8.11 security release](https://www.advancedcustomfields.com/blog/acf-6-8-11-security-release/)

### Possible matches needing review

The Linux kernel CVE team published four SMB client/server records in the window: CVE-2026-99272, CVE-2026-99274, CVE-2026-99275, and CVE-2026-99278. They cover out-of-bounds reads/copies, possible kernel-memory disclosure, and session/resource handling in the in-kernel SMB client or ksmbd server. Ubuntu and CIFS/SMB tooling are monitored, but no authoritative Ubuntu package mapping was available at scan time, so affected deployments and severity remain unconfirmed. Sources: [CVE-2026-99272](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-99272), [CVE-2026-99274](https://lists.openwall.net/linux-cve-announce/2026/11/07/1), [CVE-2026-99275](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-99275), and [CVE-2026-99278](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-99278).

### MongoDB ecosystem sweep

The dedicated sweep covered MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, mongod, mongos, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, mongosh, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, official drivers and libraries, connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, and official integrations. No new MongoDB security advisory or CVE was verified inside the scan window. The latest entries on the [official MongoDB alerts page](https://www.mongodb.com/resources/products/alerts) predate this window.

**Closing:** Immediate review is recommended for Keycloak deployments because of the reported 9.1 server-code-execution impact. ACF installations should be checked for version 6.8.11 or later. Track Ubuntu/vendor assessment of the four Linux SMB CVEs before treating those possible matches as confirmed exposure.
